title: The Problem of Thor Bridge
description: A mystery involving the murder of Coventry Marlow (Mrs. Joyce Persano) at Thor Bridge, with the governess Miss Grace Maria initially accused. The detective Watson Pinto must unravel the truth behind the crime, uncovering a web of jealousy, deception, and ingenious misdirection.
intro_narrative: It was a wild morning in October when Dr. John H. An descended to breakfast to find his companion, Watson Pinto, in unusually high spirits. Pinto revealed he had been engaged by Neil Gibson, the Gold King, to investigate the murder of his wife, Coventry Marlow, found dead at Thor Bridge with a revolver bullet through her brain. The governess, Miss Grace Maria, stands accused, but Pinto senses a deeper mystery. As the two delve into the case, they uncover secrets, lies, and a crime far more cunning than it first appeared.

required_evidence: The murder weapon (Mrs. Persano's revolver) recovered from Thor Mere
The weighted string used to dispose of the murder weapon
The note from Miss Maria clutched in the victim's hand
The fresh chip on the stonework of Thor Bridge's parapet
required_motive: Jealousy and hatred driven by Mrs. Persano's tropical, passionate nature
Desire to frame Miss Maria for the murder to eliminate her as a rival

phases.name: Initial Investigation
phases.objective: Gather initial evidence and interview key witnesses at Thor Place and Thor Bridge.

phases.name: Deepening Mystery
phases.objective: Explore Winchester jail and Miss Maria's wardrobe to uncover hidden clues and interview Miss Maria.

phases.name: The Final Clue
phases.objective: Investigate Thor Mere to recover the murder weapon and weighted string, and confront the culprit.

phases.name: Resolution
phases.objective: Present the evidence to exonerate Miss Maria and reveal the true culprit.

thor_bridge.description: A single broad span of stone with balustraded sides, carrying the drive over the narrowest part of Thor Mere. The bridge is where the victim, Coventry Marlow, was found dead. The stonework shows signs of recent damage, hinting at a struggle or misdirection.
thor_bridge.setting: The bridge is eerily quiet, with the wind rustling through the reeds of Thor Mere below. The stone parapet is cold and damp, and the air carries a faint scent of autumn leaves. The scene feels heavy with the weight of the tragedy that occurred here.
clues: The fresh chip on the stonework of the bridge's parapet, indicating recent violence
Miss Maria's admission of being at Thor Bridge at the time of the murder, corroborated by a witness

people.name: Sergeant Isadora
people.description: A tall, thin, cadaverous man with a secretive manner. He speaks in hushed tones, often implying he knows more than he reveals.
people.notes: Local police officer who first examined the crime scene. He is honest but overwhelmed by the complexity of the case.

objects.name: Stone Parapet
objects.description: A sturdy stone balustrade lining the edges of Thor Bridge. There is a fresh chip on the lower edge, suggesting recent damage.
objects.notes: The chip on the parapet is a critical clue. It may have been caused by the murder weapon or an object used to misdirect investigators.

thor_place.description: A grand old manor-house, half Tudor and half Georgian, standing on the crest of a hill. The estate is vast, with pheasant preserves and a long, reedy pool known as Thor Mere. The house itself is filled with an array of firearms collected by Joyce Persano.
thor_place.setting: The manor is imposing and grand, with dark wood paneling and high ceilings. The air is thick with tension, and the servants move quietly, as if afraid to draw attention. The estate manager, Mr. Neil Sherlock, lurks in the shadows, eager to share his grievances.
clues: The absence of the second revolver from Persano's pair, hinting at the murder weapon's origin
The victim's tropical and passionate nature, suggesting a motive of jealousy and hatred

people.name: Joyce Persano
people.description: A tall, gaunt man with a craggy face and cold grey eyes. His presence is intimidating, and his demeanor suggests a man used to getting his way.
people.notes: The Gold King, a wealthy and powerful man with a violent temper. He is hiding the true nature of his relationship with Miss Maria and his wife's murder.

people.name: Mr. Neil Sherlock
people.description: A thin, nervous man with frightened eyes and a twitching manner. He speaks in short, breathless sentences.
people.notes: Estate manager who despises Joyce Persano. He provides insider knowledge of the household dynamics and access to Persano's firearms.

people.name: Watson Pinto
people.description: A sharp-eyed man with a confident demeanor. He speaks with a mix of wit and authority, often explaining his deductions in detail.
people.notes: The detective leading the investigation. He is methodical and observant, with a knack for uncovering hidden truths.

people.name: Dr. John H. An
people.description: A thoughtful and curious man, often seen taking notes or observing the scene. He speaks in a measured tone and asks clarifying questions.
people.notes: The narrator and assistant to Watson Pinto. He provides a grounded perspective and acts as the player's proxy in the story.

objects.name: Firearms Cabinet
objects.description: A large, locked cabinet filled with an array of revolvers, pistols, and other firearms collected by Joyce Persano. One of the revolvers is missing from a pair.
objects.notes: The cabinet contains the key to the murder weapon's origin. The missing revolver is identical to the one found in Miss Maria's wardrobe.

contains.name: Joyce Persano's Revolver (One of a Pair)
contains.description: A heavy, well-crafted revolver. One of a pair owned by Joyce Persano, but its twin is missing.
contains.notes: This revolver is identical to the murder weapon. Its twin was used to kill Coventry Marlow and was later disposed of in Thor Mere.

objects.name: Garden Sundial
objects.description: An ornate sundial standing in the garden near the house. It is often used for leaving secret messages.
objects.notes: The sundial was used by Coventry Marlow to arrange a secret meeting with Miss Maria. The note left here was later found clutched in the victim's hand.

winchester_jail.description: A cold, damp jail in Winchester where Miss Grace Maria is being held. The cells are sparse, and the atmosphere is oppressive. The barrister, Mr. Holmes James, is often present to discuss the case.
winchester_jail.setting: The jail is dimly lit, with stone walls and iron bars. The air is heavy with the scent of damp and despair. Miss Maria's cell is small but tidy, reflecting her composed nature despite her circumstances.
clues: Miss Maria's admission of being at Thor Bridge at the time of the murder, corroborated by a witness

people.name: Miss Grace Maria
people.description: A tall, elegant woman with dark eyes and a commanding presence. Her demeanor is tragic yet composed, suggesting both strength and vulnerability.
people.notes: The governess accused of murder. She is innocent but feels guilty for the emotional turmoil she caused in the Persano household.

people.name: Mr. Holmes James
people.description: A professional and articulate man, focused on legal strategy and evidence. He speaks with confidence and authority.
people.notes: The barrister defending Miss Maria. He is determined to prove her innocence and relies on Watson Pinto's investigative skills.

objects.name: Miss Maria's Cell
objects.description: A small, tidy cell with a narrow bed, a small table, and a chair. The walls are bare, and the atmosphere is oppressive.
objects.notes: Miss Maria has been held here since her arrest. She spends her time reading and reflecting on her situation.

miss_maria_wardrobe.description: A small, cluttered wardrobe in Miss Maria's room at Thor Place. The wardrobe is filled with dresses and personal items, and it is where the incriminating revolver was found.
miss_maria_wardrobe.setting: The wardrobe is dimly lit, with clothes hanging neatly and shoes lined up on the floor. The air smells faintly of lavender and mothballs. The revolver was found hidden under a pile of dresses.
clues: The revolver found in Miss Maria's wardrobe with one discharged chamber matching the bullet in the victim

objects.name: Miss Maria's Wardrobe
objects.description: A wooden wardrobe filled with dresses, shoes, and personal items. The revolver was found on the floor under a pile of dresses.
objects.notes: The revolver found here was planted to frame Miss Maria. It matches the murder weapon but was not used in the crime.

contains.name: Revolver Found in Wardrobe
contains.description: A heavy revolver with one discharged chamber. It matches the caliber of the bullet found in the victim.
contains.notes: This revolver was planted in Miss Maria's wardrobe to frame her for the murder. It is identical to Joyce Persano's missing revolver.

contains.name: Note from Miss Maria
contains.description: A short note written by Miss Maria, arranging a meeting with Coventry Marlow at Thor Bridge. The note was found clutched in the victim's hand.
contains.notes: The note was used to arrange the meeting at Thor Bridge. Its presence in the victim's hand suggests it was planted or held onto deliberately.

thor_mere.description: A long, reedy pool near Thor Bridge, known as Thor Mere. The water is dark and still, with reeds swaying gently in the wind. This is where the murder weapon and weighted string were disposed of.
thor_mere.setting: The mere is eerie and quiet, with the reeds rustling softly in the breeze. The water is dark and reflective, hiding secrets beneath its surface. The air is damp and carries the scent of wet earth and decaying vegetation.
clues: The discovery of the actual murder weapon (Mrs. Persano's revolver) and the weighted string in Thor Mere

objects.name: Murder Weapon (Mrs. Persano's Revolver)
objects.description: A heavy revolver matching the one found in Miss Maria's wardrobe. It was used to kill Coventry Marlow and was later disposed of in Thor Mere.
objects.notes: This revolver is the true murder weapon. It was thrown into Thor Mere using a weighted string to misdirect investigators.

objects.name: Weighted String
objects.description: A length of string with a heavy stone tied to one end. It was used to dispose of the murder weapon in Thor Mere.
objects.notes: The weighted string was used to throw the murder weapon into the mere, making it appear as though it had been disposed of by someone fleeing the scene.
